The Stable Log Pseudo-Determinant and Its Derivative Blocks

Source: R/additive_penalty.R
additive_stable.Rd

Evaluates \(\log\mathrm{pdet}\sum_k\lambda_kP_k\) with \(\operatorname{tr}(S^{+}P_k)\) and \(\operatorname{tr}(S^{+}P_kS^{+}P_l)\) by the similarity transformation additive_sum() describes, recursing so that any number of components is served.

Usage

additive_stable(mats, lam, p_rank, d_tol = additive_tol(), r_tol = 1e-10)

Arguments

mats

The component matrices, as AdditivePenalty() stores them.

lam

The smoothing parameters, in the same order.

p_rank

The rank of the sum, fixed at construction.

d_tol

The gap at which the components are split, additive_tol() by default.

r_tol

The relative eigenvalue tolerance a group's rank is counted at, matching additive_penalty()'s own tol.

Value

A list of value (a single number), dlog (a numeric vector), d2log (a square matrix) and depth (how many levels the partition needed, a diagnostic).

Details

A rank is read from the components normalized one by one and never from the weighted sum, which is the convention additive_penalty() already follows for the rank of the whole: the null space of a sum of positive semidefinite matrices is the intersection of theirs, so a group's rank is a property of that group and its determination is well conditioned. The rank left to the next level is the current one less what the dominant group peels, so it is obtained by subtraction and never counted again.

See also

additive_sum(), which calls it and checks its answer.
